etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English slappen, of uncertain origin, possibly imitative. Compare Low German Slappe (“slap”), whence also German Schlappe (“defeat”). Compare also Italian sleppa (“slap”).

definitions.definition: (countable) A blow, especially one given with the open hand, or with something broad and flat.
(countable) A sharp percussive sound like that produced by such a blow.
(countable, music) The percussive sound produced in slap bass playing.

quote.citation: 2019 August 15, Bob Stanley, “'Groovy, groovy, groovy': listening to Woodstock 50 years on – all 38 discs”, in The Guardian‎[1]:
quote.text: Havens goes into the terrific Freedom for an encore, which will turn out to be a highlight of the movie; its chopped guitar and conga slaps pre-empt late 90s R&B.

quote.citation: 1997, James Gardiner, Who's a Pretty Boy Then?, page 123:
quote.text: Well, she schlumphed her Vera down the screech at a rate of knots, zhooshed up the riah, checked the slap in the mirror behind the bar, straightened up one ogle fake riah that had come adrift, and bold as brass orderlied over as fast as she could manage in those bats and, in her best lips, asked, if she could parker the omi a bevvy.

quote.citation: Quoted in 2006, Matt Houlbrook, Queer London (page 151)
quote.text: If you had too much slap on when you went out . . . your mates say too much slap on your ecaf. Yeah. Oh really girl? Yes . . . Go in the lavs here and have a look.

definitions.definition: (slang, countable) An eye-catching sticker used in street art.

quote.citation: 2019, Saskia Hufnagel, Duncan Chappell, The Palgrave Handbook on Art Crime, page 859:
quote.text: […]  which seek to retake public space for their own expression, using graffiti, stickering, 'slaps' and street art to dissent from the commercialisation of the public sphere.

quote.citation: 1922 October 26, Virginia Woolf, chapter 1, in Jacob’s Room, Richmond, London:  […]  Leonard & Virginia Woolf at the Hogarth Press, →OCLC; republished London: The Hogarth Press, 1960, →OCLC:
quote.text: Mrs. Flanders rose, slapped her coat this side and that to get the sand off, and picked up her black parasol.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To cause something to strike soundly.
(intransitive, stative, slang) To be excellent, especially when relating to music.

quote.citation: 2019, “Glass Battles”, in PT Music Watch, number 1, page 35:
quote.text: There are some cinematic elements, but at the end of the day, the album fucking slaps.

quote.citation: 2019 April, Gloria Perez, “Your Things”, in Your Mag, page 74:
quote.text: Also I will never get tired of the song "Motion Sickness" by Phoebe Bridgers. Shit slaps.

quote.citation: 2019 November, Elly Watson, “The Great 2019 Debate”, in DIY, page 59:
quote.text: 2016's 'Girls Like Me' still slaps to this day.

quote.citation: 2018, “The Secret Ceramics Room of Secrets”, in Bob's Burgers:
quote.text: Louise Belcher: "On Monday there was supposed to be some big schoolboard inspection or something, so instead of cleaning the place up, what does the principal do? He panics. He and the janitor and the janitor's brother slap a wall where the door used to be."Gene Belcher: "Wall slap."

definitions.definition: (transitive, informal, figurative) To impose a penalty, etc. on (someone).
(transitive, informal) To play slap bass on (an instrument).

quote.citation: 2007, Jon Paulien, The Gospel from Patmos:
quote.text: With no drums, Black began slapping his bass to keep time while Moore's guitar leaped in and out of the melody line.

quote.text: You just take my orders, Cap’n Hawkins, and we’ll sail slap in and be done with it.

quote.citation: 1864, Tony Pastor, John F. Poole, Tony Pastor's Complete Budget of Comic Songs, page 63:
quote.text: They called the tom-cat to the trap, / Who molrowed as he smelt at the door, O— / Opened his mouth and swallowed him slap, / All the while most profanely he swore, O!
